submission.justification:
Algorithm-L1 has the highest signal efficiency of the three candidates at every threshold scanned (about 86% to 93%, versus at most 87% for L2 and 74% for L3). It is also marked deployable within the L1 FPGA budget and the threshold lies inside the 20-60 GeV window.

The 34 GeV working point is weakly supported. In the refined scan, efficiency is 92.8% at 33 GeV, 93.7% at 34 GeV, 91.2% at 35 GeV and 90.9% at 36 GeV. That pattern is non-monotonic and looks like statistical fluctuation, not a real peak. Across 30-40 GeV, L1 averages about 92%, so the efficiency difference between 34 and 35 GeV is within the noise. I kept 34 GeV because it is the recorded optimum, but the choice between 30-40 GeV is not sharply determined by the simulation.

The main gap is the rate. The allocated budget is 8 kHz, but no trigger rate was recorded at any threshold. The recommendation therefore cannot be confirmed against the rate constraint. Lower thresholds generally increase the rate, so 34 GeV could exceed the 8 kHz budget. Before deployment, the rate at 34 GeV should be measured on minimum-bias or zero-bias data, and the threshold should be confirmed or raised if the rate is too high. Efficiency should also be re-checked with a larger signal sample to test whether the 34 GeV value holds.
